今天是12月20日，新年就要到了。 (Jīntiān shì shí'èr yuè èrshí rì, xīnnián jiù yào dào le.) - Today is December 20th. The New Year is coming.
新年你准备做什么？ (Xīnnián nǐ zhǔnbèi zuò shénme?) - What plans do you have for the New Year?
你买票了吗？ (Nǐ mǎi piào le ma?) - Have you bought the ticket?
还没有呢，明天就去火车站买票。 (Hái méiyǒu ne, míngtiān jiù qù huǒchēzhàn mǎi piào.) - Not yet. I'll go to the railway station to buy it tomorrow.

我不喜欢一直住在同一个城市，想去其他城市看一看。 (Wǒ bù xǐhuan yìzhí zhù zài tóng yí ge chéngshì, xiǎng qù qítā chéngshì kàn yi kàn.) - I don't like living in the same city all the time; I want to go to other cities and have a look.
现在多高了？ (Xiànzài duō gāo le?) - How tall is she now?

像她爸爸，刚出生时她爸爸高兴得一个晚上都没睡着。 (Xiàng tā bàba, gāng chūshēng shí tā bàba gāoxìng de yí ge wǎnshang dōu méi shuì zháo.) - Like her father; when she was just born her father was so happy that he didn't sleep a wink all night.
那您现在为什么不去？ (Nà nín xiànzài wèi shénme bú qù?) - Then why don't you go now?
现在钱不是问题了，主要是没有时间。 (Xiànzài qián bú shì wèntí le, zhǔyào shì méiyǒu shíjiān.) - Money is no longer a problem now; the main thing is that I have no time.
我认为现在您有时间也不会出去玩儿。 (Wǒ rènwéi xiànzài nín yǒu shíjiān yě bú huì chūqu wánr.) - I think that even if you had time now, you wouldn't go out to have fun.
你说得对，我现在累得下了班就想睡觉。 (Nǐ shuō de duì, wǒ xiànzài lèi de xiàle bān jiù xiǎng shuì jiào.) - You're right; I'm now so tired that after work I just want to sleep.
谢谢你们来看我女儿。 (Xièxiè nǐmen lái kàn wǒ nǚ'ér.) - Thank you for coming to see my daughter.
谁都有办法看好你的“病” (Shéi dōu yǒu bànfǎ kànhǎo nǐ de “bìng”) - Everybody is able to cure your “disease”
爱好 àihào (hobby, interest)
办法 bànfǎ (way, approach)

当然是春天，天气不那么冷了，草和树都绿了，花也开了。 (Dāngrán shì chūntiān, tiānqì bú nàme lěng le, cǎo hé shù dōu lǜ le, huā yě kāi le.) - Spring, of course: the weather is not so cold, the grass and trees have turned green, and flowers have bloomed.
我最喜欢夏天，因为我可以穿漂亮的裙子了。 (Wǒ zuì xǐhuan xiàtiān, yīnwèi wǒ kěyǐ chuān piàoliang de qúnzi le.) - I like summer best, because I can wear pretty skirts.
那我也喜欢夏天了。 (Nà wǒ yě xǐhuan xiàtiān le.) - Then I like summer too.
怎么？你也有漂亮的裙子？ (Zěnme? Nǐ yě yǒu piàoliang de qúnzi?) - What? Do you also have pretty skirts?
不，我喜欢看你穿漂亮的裙子。 (Bù, wǒ xǐhuan kàn nǐ chuān piàoliang de qúnzi.) - No, I like seeing you wear pretty skirts.
前几天有点儿发烧，现在好多了。 (Qián jǐ tiān yǒudiǎnr fā shāo, xiànzài hǎoduō le.) - I had a bit of a fever a few days ago; I'm much better now.
我现在没钱了。 (Wǒ xiànzài méi qián le.) - I don't have money now (I used to).
上个月很冷，现在天气不那么冷了。 (Shàng gè yuè hěn lěng, xiànzài tiānqì bú nàme lěng le.) - It was very cold last month; now the weather is not so cold.
我前几天有点儿发烧，现在好多了。 (Wǒ qián jǐ tiān yǒudiǎnr fāshāo, xiànzài hǎo duō le.) - I had a bit of a fever a few days ago; now I'm much better.
我现在喜欢夏天了。 (Wǒ xiànzài xǐhuan xiàtiān le.) - I like summer now.
这条裙子是去年买的，今年就不能穿了。 (Zhè tiáo qúnzi shì qùnián mǎi de, jīnnián jiù bù néng chuān le.) - I bought this skirt last year and can't wear it this year.
我最近有点儿累。 (Wǒ zuìjìn yǒudiǎnr lèi.) - I am a bit tired lately.

Lesson 19 Text 1: 在家 (At home)
女儿最近喜欢把头发放在耳朵后面，你知道为什么吗？ (Nǚ'ér zuìjìn xǐhuan bǎ tóufa fàng zài ěrduo hòumiàn, nǐ zhīdào wèi shénme ma?) - Our daughter likes to put her hair behind her ears lately; do you know why?

HSK L2 Page 60 (Culture: Table Manners)

中国人无论在家还是在饭馆，多人聚餐时一般会坐圆形餐桌，这样大家都可以面对面。 (Zhōngguórén wúlùn zài jiā háishi zài fànguǎn, duō rén jùcān shí yìbān huì zuò yuánxíng cānzhuō, zhèyàng dàjiā dōu kěyǐ miànduìmiàn.) - Chinese people prefer round tables when dining, no matter at home or in a restaurant, so that all can sit face-to-face.

在饭馆里入座的时候，主人的右手边是主客，左手边是次重要的客人。 (Zài fànguǎn li rùzuò de shíhou, zhǔrén de yòushǒu biān shì zhǔkè, zuǒshǒu biān shì cì zhòngyào de kèrén.) - Seated in a restaurant, the host has the main guest on his right hand and the second-most important guest on his left.
主人对面上菜的位置一般不能给客人坐。 (Zhǔrén duìmiàn shàng cài de wèizhi yìbān bù néng gěi kèrén zuò.) - The seat opposite to the host, where dishes are served, usually cannot be offered to a guest.
通过餐桌上的菜也可以分辨主客。 (Tōngguò cānzhuō shang de cài yě kěyǐ fēnbiàn zhǔkè.) - One can tell the host from the guest through the dishes also.

如果有鱼，鱼头要对着最主要的客人，表示主人对客人的尊重。 (Rúguǒ yǒu yú, yú tóu yào duìzhe zuì zhǔyào de kèrén, biǎoshì zhǔrén duì kèrén de zūnzhòng.) - If there is a fish dish on the table, the head of the fish should point to the most important guest to show the host's respect for the guest.

Culture Note: Taboo Gifts in China

在中国，有一些东西不能当作礼物送给别人，比如：伞、鞋、钟表等等。 (Zài Zhōngguó, yǒu yìxiē dōngxi bù néng dàngzuò lǐwù sòng gěi biérén, bǐrú: sǎn, xié, zhōngbiǎo děngděng.) - In China, some things cannot be given to others as gifts, such as umbrellas, shoes and clocks.
“鞋”与“邪”的发音相同，有倒霉的意思。 (“Xié” yǔ “xié” de fāyīn xiāngtóng, yǒu dǎoméi de yìsi.) - 鞋 (shoe) sounds the same as 邪 (evil), which means bad luck.

“送钟”与“送终”发音相同，有将去世之人送走的意思。 (“Sòng zhōng” yǔ “sòng zhōng” fāyīn xiāngtóng, yǒu jiāng qùshì zhī rén sòngzǒu de yìsi.) - Giving a clock (送钟) sounds exactly the same as attending upon a dying person (送终), implying seeing off a person who has passed away.
